jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Probing Nanoscale Heterogeneity in Ultrafast Phase Transitions
jobs.employer_name: Natural Sciences - Institut for Fysik og Astronomi
jobs.description:
The Department of Physics, Aarhus University, invites applications for a 2-year full-time postdoc position in the project “Probing nanoscale heterogeneity in ultrafast phase transitions”.

The position is available from 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project
This project will use a recently developed soft X-ray imaging method to probe the dynamics of light-induced phase transitions at the nanoscale using X-ray Free Electron Lasers. The work will also combine lab-based experiments on time-resolved nonlinear optics.

Job responsibilities
The postdoc will be expected to:

• Lead XFEL and synchrotron experiments in soft X-ray imaging
• Prepare and characterise samples
• Lead experiments in nonlinear optics in the laboratory
Qualifications
Applicants must have:

• A PhD degree in Physics, Chemistry or a related field
• Experience with ultrafast lasers and/or X-rays and/or quantum materials
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Ny Munkegade 120, 8000 Aarhus C, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Further information
For further information about the position, please contact: Simon Wall, simon.wall@phys.au.dk.

Application deadline
The application deadline is 16 December 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. We focus on competency development and career clarification and want to make your opportunities transparent. On our website, you can find information on all types of scientific positions, as well as the entry criteria we use when assessing candidates. You can also read more about how we can assist you in your career planning and development.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.description:
Are you ready to take ownership of an experienced sales team and drive its commercial performance to the next level in a specialised Nordic technology business? Since 1988, the company has built its market position through strong supplier partnerships, deep technical expertise and long-term customer relationships. Today, Ramcon employs approximately 80 employees across Denmark and Sweden and operates from offices in Birkerød, Aarhus, Stockholm and Gothenburg.

Lead a specialised sales team

The role also carries responsibility for maintaining a strong sales culture, ensuring structured sales execution and supporting key strategic business opportunities.

Key responsibilities include:

• Leadership, coaching and development of six Product Specialists

• Sales strategy implementation and commercial development

• Budgeting, forecasting and pipeline management

• Development of strategic customer and supplier relationships

• Support of larger and strategically important sales opportunities

• Driving commercial excellence and sales performance

Commercial leadership with strategic influence

The Sales Manager will play a key role in ensuring continued growth and organizational development. Success in the position requires an ability to combine strategic perspective with operational execution while creating engagement, accountability and performance across the organization.

The position offers significant influence on the future commercial development of the business and close collaboration with customers, suppliers, and internal stakeholders across the organisation.

Your profile

The ideal candidate is an experienced commercial leader with a proven track record of creating results through strong sales leadership and structured execution. Experience from a specialised technical B2B environment is considered an advantage.

Furthermore, the successful candidate is expected to have:

• Experience leading specialist sales teams

• Strong commercial and business development capabilities

• Experience managing complex sales processes involving multiple stakeholders

• A coaching and performance-oriented leadership style

• The ability to build trust across customers, suppliers and internal stakeholders

Experience from Life Science, Diagnostics, Laboratory Solutions, Medical Technology or a related technical industry would be considered very beneficial.

If you want to learn more about this position, please do not hesitate to contact Senior Research Consultant, Tobias Møller Simonsen at +45 70 20 12 75. Please submit your CV as soon as possible, if you are interested. Please note that all enquiries will be handled with confidentiality and that we will reply to the email address from which you send your CV.

jobs.occupation: Senior Data & Analytics Engineer
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about creating value through a data-driven approach? Do you have experience being a Data Analytics Engineer?

If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new Data Analytics Engineer in the Data & Analytics team.

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease and Oncology portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

We are seeking a passionate Data Analytics Engineer to join our team. You will work closely with stakeholders and colleagues to design, build and operate data and analytics solutions that help drive better decisions across the business.

As part of a highly collaborative team, you will have the opportunity to work across the full lifecycle of a solution, from early stakeholder dialogue and requirements gathering through design, development, enablement and support. We value curiosity, ownership and collaboration, and we believe the best solutions are created together.

You will report directly to People Leader, Babak Bajelan, and Functional Leader, Henrik Aagaard Linnemann, both based in Hellerup. You will also be based on Hellerup.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Partner with stakeholders to understand needs, facilitate workshops and shape fit-for-purpose data and analytics solutions

• Design, build and operate end-to-end solutions, from data pipelines, integrations and transformations to semantic models, dashboards and reporting

• Collaborate with colleagues and users to continuously improve solutions, controls and ways of working

Qualifications and Skills:

Your background may come from data engineering, analytics engineering, business intelligence, software development or a related field. While 5+ years of experience within Data & Analytics is preferred, what matters most is your ability to translate business needs into practical solutions and collaborate effectively with stakeholders.

To succeed in the role, you should bring:

• A structured approach to testing, documentation, data quality and change management.

• Strong stakeholder and collaboration skills, with the ability to turn business needs into clear and maintainable solutions

It would also be an advantage if you have experience with:

• Modern data and development tools such as Databricks, dbt, Visual Studio Code, Azure DevOps, Git and CI/CD

• Power BI

• An understanding of working in a regulated and compliance-focused environment

You do not need to match every technology listed. We value curiosity, sound judgement and the ability to learn and develop with the team.

Key competencies:

The right team fit is central to this role. We are looking for someone who is:

• Proactive, structured and comfortable taking ownership

• A strong collaborator who enjoys working with both technical and non-technical stakeholders

• Curious, pragmatic and eager to learn and share knowledge with others

• Positive, down-to-earth and someone who enjoys contributing to a collaborative team culture

Travel: 10-15 days per year.

Office: Tuborg Boulevard 12, 2900 Hellerup

Apply now.

We evaluate applications when received, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we conduct interviews on a rolling basis and reserve the right to remove the job posting at any time.

To ensure your application is reviewed, please submit it through the specified platform - applications sent by email or other channels will not be evaluated.

For more details about the position or the company, please contact Alexander Synnes, asy@ascendispharma.com or Babak Bajelan, bab@ascendispharma.com

You can learn more about Ascendis by visiting our website www.ascendispharma.com

Applications must be submitted in English and will be treated confidentially.

As the summer holiday period approaches, you may experience a longer response time than usual. We truly appreciate your patience and thank you for your understanding. We look forward to reviewing your application as soon as possible.

A note to recruiters:

We do not allow external search party solicitation. Presentation of candidates without written permission from the Ascendis Pharma HR team (specifically from: Talent Acquisition Partner or Human Resources Director) is not allowed. If this occurs, your ownership of these candidates will not be acknowledged.

jobs.occupation: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy
jobs.description:
Declaration of interest regarding PhD project:

The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology.
We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences.

 

Research environment

The PhD student will be based in the research group of Applied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenology in the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research.

The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad.

The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology.

 

Project description

The PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led by Anthony Vincent Fernandez. The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1st, 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists.

The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset.

In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties.

The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. Additional funds may be available.

 

Qualifications

Before the start date of September 1st, 2027, the applicant should have a master’s degree in philosophy or a related field and total course credits equivalent to 300 ECTS. Typically, this is a total of at least five years of education combined between bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with 60 ECTS obtained for every full year of study.

The candidate should have a background in philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, and/or phenomenology. Familiarity with qualitative research methods (especially analysis methods) is an advantage, but by no means required.

The candidate should be proficient in English. Proficiency in Danish or another Scandinavian language may be an advantage, but is not required.

For further information about the project, please contact:
Anthony Vincent Fernandez

Department of Psychology

University of Southern Denmark (SDU)

E-mail: afernandez@health.sdu.dk

Please note that while we are happy to provide answers to questions about the position and application process, direct feedback on application materials cannot be provided.

Applications must include (in English, or with a certified English translation):

 

• 
A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”.

• 
Detailed CV, including personal contact information as well as any publications or presentations

• 
Certified copy of diploma and transcripts (Master’s degree in a relevant field). If the applicant is in the process of completing their master’s degree, they should provide transcripts along with a letter from their supervisor confirming expected completion of their degree before September 1st, 2027.

• 
Writing sample of maximum 10,000 words (e.g., publication, conference paper, selection from a master’s thesis). If the sample exceeds this length, please indicate which section should be read.

• 
A document listing 2-3 references, with contact information and a brief note about your relation to the reference. Note that reference letters will only be requested for candidates invited to interview.

 

At this stage, no project proposal is required. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to prepare a brief project plan.

Please do not use generative AI in the formulation of any application materials. The purpose of these materials is to gain a clear sense of you and your abilities.

Shortlisting and interviews may be used in the assessment process.
 

For purposes of evaluation and assessment, application materials may be shared with external members of the project team at Aarhus University and Amsterdam University Medical Center.

Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated

 

Closing date January 15th, 2027

 

We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date.
Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students.
 

The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order)

 

Salary and Working Conditions at SDU

PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.

Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98   per year.

The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future.

As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.description:
Are you structured, analytical, and motivated by ensuring that products are available when our customers need them?

We are looking for a Demand Planner to support the daily planning and replenishment of our warehouse assortment and help ensure the right balance between product availability and inventory.

In this role, you will work hands-on with demand forecasts, replenishment, purchase orders, inventory levels, and planning exceptions. You will be an important link between Sales, Procurement, Warehouse, Operations, and our suppliers and factories, helping turn demand into clear and executable supply requirements.

Your key responsibilities

• 
Maintain and update demand forecasts based on sales history, trends, customer input, and changes in demand.

• 
Plan replenishment and ensure timely ordering of products for our warehouse assortment.

• 
Follow up on open purchase orders, delivery dates, and expected incoming supply.

• 
Monitor stock levels and identify potential shortages, excess inventory, and availability risks.

• 
React to changes in demand and supply and adjust plans accordingly.

• 
Follow up on service level, forecast accuracy, inventory, and other operational planning KPIs.

• 
Work closely with Sales, Procurement, Warehouse, and Operations to resolve day-to-day planning and availability issues.

• 
Maintain high-quality planning parameters and master data.

• 
Support improvements to planning processes, systems, and ways of working.

Who are you?

You have experience within demand planning, replenishment, purchasing, inventory management, or supply chain planning and enjoy working in a role where you are close to the daily operation.

You are comfortable working with numbers, data, and planning systems and have a structured approach to managing priorities and following up on deviations. Experience with ERP systems, forecasting or replenishment tools, and Excel is an advantage.

As a person, you are structured, proactive, persistent, and solution-oriented. You take ownership of your area, follow issues through to resolution, and communicate clearly with colleagues and stakeholders.

What we offer

You will join an international planning organization and take responsibility for an important part of our daily planning operation. Your work will have a direct impact on product availability, inventory levels, and customer service.

You will work closely with colleagues across Sales, Procurement, Logistics, Warehouse, and Operations and have opportunities to develop your competencies within demand and supply chain planning.

The position is based in Tvis, Holstebro.

Recruitment process

Please submit your application and CV via our recruitment system. Interviews will be conducted on an ongoing basis.

Integrating Hormonal and Biomechanical Stimuli in Multi-scale Modelling of human Vascular cells

Research area and project description:
As part of the ERC Starting Grant project DISSEX, which aims at developing a sex-aware multiscale framework to predict vascular dissection risk, we are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join our multi-disciplinary Cardiovascular Engineering (CareEng) group at Aarhus University. This PhD project specifically aims at quantifying how human coronary arteries respond to systemic hormonal fluctuations and biomechanical stress through both experimental and computational techniques. There are 2 objectives.

Objective 1: Experimental investigation of vascular adaptation
The candidate will use innovative microfluidic platforms and ex vivo human coronary arteries to recreate physiological and pathological vascular environments. By exposing vascular tissues to controlled flow, pressure, and hormone profiles representative of daily fluctuations in estradiol, cortisol, and testosterone, the project will quantify how endothelial and smooth muscle cells respond in terms of proliferation, apoptosis, signalling, and biomechanical function. Particular attention will be given to endothelial pathways involving nitric oxide and endothelin-1, providing a unique dataset on how systemic and mechanical stimuli jointly influence vascular health.

Objective 2: Development of a multiscale computational model
Building on the experimental findings, the candidate will develop a multiscale computational framework linking cellular activity to vessel-scale biomechanics. Combining agent-based modelling with computational fluid dynamics, the model will integrate hormonal regulation, cellular adaptation, and biomechanical stresses within the vascular wall. The resulting digital platform will enable mechanistic investigation of vascular remodelling processes and provide a foundation for understanding conditions that may predispose arteries to dissection.

The PhD candidate will join an interdisciplinary team bringing together expertise in vascular physiology, Cardiovascular biomechanics, microfluidics and fabrication; computational modelling, and clinical cardiovascular medicine. The project includes close collaboration with clinicians, biologists, and engineers and provides access to state-of-the-art laboratory and computational research facilities.

Qualifications and specific competences:
We are looking for highly motivated and independent candidates with the intention to complete a 3-year PhD at Aarhus University. The ideal candidate is expected to have most of the following qualifications:
 
• Master’s degree in Biomedical Engineering, Biomechanical Engineering, Biotechnology or relevant fields.
• In-depth knowledge in fluid mechanics and cardiovascular applications.
• Experience with cell culture and tissue engineering
• Familiarity with numerical modelling (CFD), and software such as COMSOL, SimVascular, or similar software
• (optional) Previous exposure to agent-based modelling or systems biology
• excellent written and spoken English (optional Danish).

Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering, Aarhus University, Katrinebjergvej 89F, 8200 Aarhus N.

• Conducting research through externally sponsored grants at national and international levels.
• Establishing relevant collaborations with the Danish industry.
• Contributing to the operation of the department.
Your profile
We are looking for a candidate that can enhance the department’s competencies in computational design. The candidate shall hold:

• Engineering background (B.Sc. and M.Sc.).
• Doctoral degree in a relevant field of research.
• High-level proficiency in English.
The following qualifications and experience are required:

• Scientific computing, possibly with different programming languages (e.g., Python, Julia, C#, C++ MATLAB).
• Parametric and algorithmic building design using, e.g., Rhino/Grasshopper tool suite.
• Physics-informed machine learning, generative and agentic AI for building design automation.
• Teaching and developing computational and generative design courses related to structural engineering.
• Supervision of undergraduate and graduate students (B.Sc., M.Sc., and Ph.D. theses).
Candidates must demonstrate potential for outstanding research and teaching. The selected candidate shall demonstrate:

• Some years of post-graduate research and publication experience are required. A pre-existing and growing international research network is expected. Prior collaboration with the Danish innovation ecosystem is desired, but not essential.
• Experience from successful external research collaborations with industry and academia, project management skills. Experience in the attraction of external funding is preferred.
• Research ability documented through rising publication and citation records evidenced by appropriate bibliometric parameters in reputable international peerreviewed journals.
Well-defined research focus and sound strategy to develop a research group.

Who we are
The Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering at Aarhus University is a growing engineering environment with a clear vision for the future of the built environment.

Established in 2021, the department today includes more than 100 researchers and educators and around 1.050 students. We conduct research and education within structural engineering, geotechnics, architectural engineering and design, sustainability, construction management, climate adaptation, indoor climate, building materials, and digital technologies.

The construction sector is facing major challenges related to climate, resource consumption, and the way we design and build our cities and buildings.

Through research, education, and collaboration with industry and public-sector partners, we contribute to developing technological solutions that support a more sustainable built environment.

Our research and development activities are closely connected to the needs of industry and society, and many projects are carried out in collaboration with companies, public authorities, and other research environments. This ensures that the knowledge and technologies developed at the department are relevant in practice and create value beyond the university.

Education is a central part of the department’s identity. We offer Bachelor’s, Master’s, and PhD programmes in engineering and continuously work to improve the connection between research, teaching, and practice.

Across our programmes, students work with real-world challenges, current technologies, and sustainable solutions for the construction sector.

What we offer
We offer an innovative and collaborative teaching and research environment with close interaction between students, researchers, and industry partners. The department provides well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories, and access to shared technical facilities. We offer an interdisciplinary environment with national, international, and industrial collaborators. Our academic environment is built on collaboration, knowledge sharing, and professional dialogue. The workplace is characterised by professionalism, flexibility, and a healthy work–life balance. The department is located at Navitas on the waterfront in Aarhus, Denmark

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is at Navitas, Inge Lehmanns Gade 10, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark. The area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Associate Professor, Giuseppe Abbiati +45 93 52 17 51, abbiati@cae.au.dk.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than December 14 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range 
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

A company vehicle to take home and no on-call duties
At Bravida, you will join a team of skilled, dedicated technicians who take pride in their work.

jobs.occupation: Content and Creative Specialist (Part-Time)
jobs.description:
Are you a strong writer with an eye for design and a practical approach to using artificial intelligence?

Can you keep a website fresh, turn ideas into engaging social content, and build workflows that make content production more efficient?

Patiro is looking for a part-time Content and Creative Specialist to manage and develop our content across our website, social media, press releases, and external profiles. You will help us communicate clearly, maintain a consistent brand, and reach the right audiences.

Your responsibilities

You will help us:

• Plan and maintain a content calendar across our channels.

• Write, edit, publish, and update website content, social media posts, press releases, and other communications.

• Keep company listings, directories, and relevant registers accurate and up to date.

• Create visuals and reusable templates in Figma or similar design tools.

• Refine our brand guidelines and apply them consistently across content and design.

• Follow and develop our voice and tone guidelines, adapting communication to different audiences.

• Use artificial intelligence and automation tools, such as Make.com, to improve content workflows, approvals, publishing, and distribution.

• Repurpose content into formats suited to different channels and audiences.

• Improve content discoverability across search engines and artificial intelligence search and answer platforms.

• Track content performance and use the findings to improve topics, formats, and distribution.

• Coordinate with internal experts to ensure content is accurate, relevant, and ready for publication.

What we are looking for

You are someone who:

• Has experience creating and managing content across websites and social media.

• Writes clear, engaging English and can turn complex subjects into accessible stories.

• Has a strong visual eye and practical experience with Figma or similar tools.

• Can share examples of content and creative work you have produced.

• Has hands-on experience using artificial intelligence and automation tools to improve workflows while maintaining editorial quality.

• Understands how content can support awareness, engagement, and action.

• Keeps up with developments in search engine optimisation and content visibility across large language models, generative search, and answer engines.

• Works independently, manages priorities, and takes content from initial idea through publication and review.

• Checks facts carefully and handles sensitive topics with sound judgement.

Technical search optimisation skills are welcome, but are not required. We value strong editorial judgement, creative ability, and the ability to put useful tools into practice.

Additional experience we would value

• Healthcare, clinical research, or patient-facing communications.

• Press releases, media outreach, or corporate communications.

• Content management systems and publishing tools.

• Short-form video creation and editing.

• Community management and audience engagement.

• Content analytics and testing different messages or creative formats.

About the role

You will work closely with our leadership, marketing, and medical teams to build a consistent and credible presence for Patiro. We are looking for someone who can contribute ideas and take ownership of the daily work needed to keep our content relevant and our channels active.

Hours: 5-15 hours per weekStart date: As soon as possible

How to apply

Send your application, a short introduction, and examples of your writing and visual work to the email below.

Please also share an example of how you have used artificial intelligence or automation to improve a content workflow, including your role and the result.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Apply via this e-mail

careers@patiro.com
